key_insight: The paper shows that biomedical AI explanations can be made machine-checkable by linking radiomic features to explicit evidence records, so claims can be verified independently of model predictions.
clinical_relevance: This could help make AI-supported imaging reports more auditable and trustworthy in neuro-oncology, especially when explanations must be tied to patient-specific MRI evidence.
method: Aligned UPenn-GBM radiomics with de novo CaPTk feature extraction from standardized MRI and expert-validated segmentations.
Built a neuro-semantic verification framework with 1,728 features across T1, T1GD, T2, and FLAIR from three tumor regions.
Tested transportability, provenance, deterministic claim checking, controlled performance degradation, and an LLM claim-extraction pilot.
evidence_signal: Median semantic-state agreement was 0.786, the verifier reached 100% exact-set accuracy on 6,620 corrupted claims, and the LLM pilot reproduced 72/72 atomic claims with 24/24 verified conditions.
watch_item: The framework verifies consistency, but it does not guarantee strong clinical prediction performance, and external MGMT discrimination was weak (ROC AUC 0.543).
paper_title: Evidence-Bound Reasoning: Neuro-Semantic Verification of Biomedical AI in Glioblastoma Radiogenomics
